claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances. Let me begin with the basics:

**What is your current residency status in the UK?** For example, are you a British citizen, a settled or pre-settled resident, or do you have another immigration status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK. I have one child, Alex, who's 4 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you're a British citizen living in the UK with Alex, who is 4 years old.

Before I can make a full assessment, I need to understand a bit more about Alex's living arrangements:

**Does Alex live with you full-time?** Or does Alex spend time living with someone else as well?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you! Now let me gather a bit more information to complete the picture.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?** (For example, at school or in an apprenticeship)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is only 4, so he's not in school yet - just at home with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Just one more question to make sure I have all the details:

**Is Alex currently in hospital or residential care?** Or is Alex living at home with you as normal?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex was in care for a little while - just a couple of months earlier this year - but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have an important follow-up question about Alex's time in care:

**When Alex was in care earlier this year, were you still considered to be responsible for him?** For instance, did you retain parental responsibility, or was the local authority or another organization considered responsible for him during that period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I still had parental responsibility for Alex during that time. It was a temporary arrangement, but I was still his parent throughout.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now I have enough information to assess your eligibility. Let me first review the official Child Benefit eligibility rules to ensure I'm applying them correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I now have all the information I need to make a decision. Based on the official eligibility rules and the information you've provided, I can assess your situation.

You meet the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit:
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex, who is 4 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you full-time

Regarding Alex's time in care earlier this year: According to the government guidance, Child Benefit payments can continue when a child is in care if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, or if there are other exceptions (such as you regularly spending money on them). Since Alex was only in care for a couple of months and has now returned home to live with you full-time, and you retained parental responsibility throughout, this temporary period does not prevent your eligibility.

Let me now provide my final eligibility determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the core requirements:
- ✓ You're a British citizen living in the UK
- ✓ You're responsible for Alex (under 16 years old)
- ✓ Alex lives with you full-time

The temporary period of care earlier this year does not affect your eligibility, as you retained parental responsibility throughout and Alex is now living with you full-time.

If you haven't already done so, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government website. If you have any further questions, feel free to ask!
